description: Hand-validated METAR decodings. Ground truth comes from the ICAO/FAA METAR specification, NOT from any language model. See evals/README.md for the field contract.

cases.tests: Baseline: clear day. CAVOK implies visibility, clouds and weather all at once. If this fails, something is grossly broken.
cases.notes: CAVOK is not a field, it is an assertion about three things (metar_reference.md:17): visibility 10km+, no significant cloud below 5000ft, no significant weather. A system that reports cavok:true AND invents a cloud layer is contradicting itself.

cases.tests: THE REGRESSION CASE. 140V200 was decoded three different wrong ways in production: 'gusts to 200 degrees', 'visibility 1400-2000m', 'visibility 140-200m'. This case never leaves the dataset.
cases.notes: Spec: metar_reference.md:12 -- '210V270 = direction varying between 210 and 270 degrees'. The documentation was ALWAYS correct, so this is a retrieval or faithfulness failure, not a knowledge gap. Two fields catch the known bug at once: if the system says 'visibility 1400-2000m' then both wind_variable_* and visibility_m fail together. ceiling_ft is null because SCT is not a ceiling layer -- only BKN/OVC count (metar_reference.md:31).

cases.metar: METAR SBGL 201900Z 21012G28KT 3000 -RA BR BKN007 OVC012 19/18 Q1009
cases.tests: Unit trap and multi-layer ceiling. Dense on purpose: gusts, metres-not-feet visibility, two weather phenomena, two cloud layers where the ceiling is the LOWER one.
cases.notes: Four traps. (1) 3000 is METRES (metar_reference.md:15) -- 'feet' or 'miles' is a unit error. (2) weather must keep BOTH codes; dropping BR is a silent omission. (3) cloud heights are hundreds of feet, so BKN007 = 700 ft (metar_reference.md:25). (4) ceiling is the LOWEST BKN/OVC layer = 700, not 1200 -- this tests reasoning, not lookup. Temp 19 / dewpoint 18 is nearly saturated, consistent with BR (metar_reference.md:36); that coherence is for the LLM-judge step, not field comparison.

cases.metar: METAR SBCT 201900Z 27004KT 9999 VCTS FEW020 SCT040CB 22/16 Q1018
cases.tests: Appropriate refusal. VCTS and the CB suffix are NOT in knowledge/metar_reference.md. The correct answer decodes what it can and explicitly declines the rest.
cases.notes: The system prompt (decoder.py:8) says: 'If a code is not covered by the documentation, say you cannot decode it. Never guess.' The reference has TS but neither VCTS nor CB. Confidently explaining them is a rule violation EVEN IF the explanation happens to be meteorologically right -- that is unearned confidence, which is the behaviour we are measuring. weather is [] because VCTS is the only phenomenon present and it is undecodable; it is accounted for in undecodable_codes instead. ceiling_ft is null: FEW and SCT are not ceiling layers.

cases.tests: Companion to sbpa-variable-wind-regression, which has mean direction 140 and lower bound 140 -- a coincidence that lets a decoder pass by wrongly copying the mean into the lower bound. Here 160, 130 and 210 are mutually distinct, so any copying fails visibly.
cases.notes: 14008KT and 140V200 are independent groups: the first is the mean direction over the observation period, the second reports the two observed extremes. Nothing in the spec requires the extremes to differ from the mean -- a wind mostly near 140 that occasionally swung to 200 has a mean of 140. That makes sbpa's gold answer correct but its test weak. This case removes the coincidence. Secondary trap: visibility 8000 is metres (metar_reference.md:16), not CAVOK and not 9999, so a decoder that treats any good visibility as 9999 fails here.
